Lalmohan Babu.description: A popular thriller writer and friend of Feluda, known for his melodramatic stories and pen name Jatayu.

Feluda.description: A private investigator and the protagonist of the stories, known for his sharp intellect and deductive skills.

Indranarayan Acharya.description: Indranarayan Acharya is a talented playwright, songwriter, and violinist associated with Bharat Opera, whose life and work become central to the investigation. He faces a dilemma about whether to leave his long-time association with Bharat Opera for a rival theatre group.

Devnarayan.description: Indranarayan Acharya's elder brother, a businessman.

Kandarpanarayan Acharya.description: Kandarpanarayan Acharya is Indranarayan Acharya's great-grandfather, known for his lavish lifestyle and travels to England and France.

Srinath.description: A character who brings tea during the meeting with Mr Acharya.

Bharat Opera.description: A well-known jatra group that stages Bengali folk theatre performances.

Surya Toran.description: The title of the jatra play staged by Bharat Opera and written by Indranarayan Acharya.

Bosepukur.description: A locality referenced as the ancestral home of the Acharya family.

England.description: A country in Europe, referenced as the place where Kandarpanarayan Acharya traveled and lived lavishly.

Prince Dwarkanath Tagore.description: A historical Bengali figure known for his wealth and westernized lifestyle, used as a comparison for Kandarpanarayan Acharya.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in India where the story is set.

Muhammad Shafi Lane.description: A street in Calcutta where the Bharat Opera office and rehearsals are located.

Beadon Street.description: A street in Calcutta, near Muhammad Shafi Lane, mentioned as part of the setting.

Charminar.description: A popular Indian cigarette brand smoked by Feluda.

jatra.description: A traditional Bengali folk theatre form, often performed in rural areas with music, drama, and dance.

barrister.description: A type of lawyer, especially one entitled to practice as an advocate in higher courts.

chartered accountant.description: A professional accountant with certification, recognized for expertise in accounting and finance.

Ashwini Bhaur.description: Ashwini Bhaur is the manager of Binapani Opera, who is trying to persuade Indranarayan to join his theatre group.

Santosh.description: The bearer who delivers a slip announcing Ashwini Bhaur's arrival.

Samrat Ashok.description: The title of a play written by Indranarayan, likely referencing the historical Indian emperor Ashoka.

Binapani Opera.description: Binapani Opera is a rival jatra company competing with Bharat Opera, also involved in the investigation and trying to recruit Indranarayan.

Nobo Natya.description: Another, smaller theatre group interested in recruiting Indranarayan.

New Opera.description: A theatre group mentioned in the context of another playwright's career move.

Sanjay Kumar.description: A playwright or theatre professional referenced as having switched theatre groups.

Babu.description: A respectful term of address in India, often used for gentlemen or elders.

Acharya.description: A title of respect in India, traditionally used for learned persons or teachers.

Monilal Poddar.description: Inspector Monilal Poddar is a local police inspector involved in the investigation of the Acharya household burglary, who knows Feluda and provides information about the case.

Pradyumna Mallik.description: Pradyumna Mallik is Keertinarayan's secretary and a writer currently working on a biography of Kandarpanarayan Acharya, assisting in the investigation.

Leena.description: Hari's daughter, who was very attached to Indranarayan.

Rohini Babu.description: Lalmohan Babu's neighbor, who knows the Acharya family and comments on their strange relationships.

Jodu Naskar Lane.description: A lane behind the Acharya house, mentioned as a possible route for the killer.

Pushpak Rath.description: The name given by Kandarpanarayan to his first Lagonda car, referencing the mythical flying chariot from Indian epics.

Sudarshan Chakra.description: A mythological weapon associated with Lord Vishnu, here used humorously as a name for a gramophone record.

Ambassador.description: A classic Indian car model, owned by Lalmohan Babu.

Puja.description: Refers to the Hindu religious festival season during which the events take place.

kurta-pyjama.description: A traditional Indian outfit consisting of a long tunic (kurta) and loose trousers (pyjama).

chowkidar.description: A watchman or guard, typically employed to look after a building or property.

bearer.description: A household servant, often responsible for serving food and attending to guests.

settee.description: A long upholstered seat for more than one person; a sofa.

veranda.description: A roofed platform along the outside of a house, level with the ground floor.

Hukum Chand.description: A mysterious name found on a piece of paper, possibly connected to the case.

France.description: A European country visited by Kandarpanarayan.

London.description: The capital city of England, visited by Kandarpanarayan.

Paris.description: The capital city of France, visited by Kandarpanarayan.

French Riviera.description: A famous coastal region in southeastern France, known for its casinos and luxury.

Mecca.description: A city in Saudi Arabia, used metaphorically here to mean a central or important place for gamblers.

Kantipur.description: A location in East Bengal where the Acharyas had their zamindari (landholding).

East Bengal.description: A region in the eastern part of Bengal, now part of Bangladesh.

Stockwell Tea Company.description: A company where Devnarayan works as a senior officer.

Skinner & Hardwick.description: A company where Harinarayan works as a chartered accountant.

Saturday Club.description: A social club frequented by Harinarayan.

Bengal Club.description: A prestigious social club frequented by Devnarayan.

Calcutta Girls’ School.description: An educational institution in Calcutta attended by Leena.

Pune.description: A city in western India where Devnarayan's married daughter lives.

National Library.description: A major library in India where Mr Mallik conducted research.

lassi.description: A traditional Indian yogurt-based drink, often sweet or flavored.

lakhs.description: A unit in the Indian numbering system equal to one hundred thousand (100,000).

zamindari.description: A system of landholding and revenue collection in India, historically involving large estates.

Suresh Mallik Street.description: A street in the city where one of the jatra companies is located.

Sarat Bhattacharya.description: Sarat Bhattacharya, also known as Sarat Babu, is the proprietor of Bharat Opera, deeply affected by the murder of his company's key artist.

Chowringhee.description: A famous area in Kolkata, known for its restaurants and cultural landmarks.

harmonium.description: A free-reed keyboard instrument, commonly used in Indian music and theatre.

almirah.description: A cupboard or wardrobe, often used in Indian households for storage.

Serampore.description: A town in West Bengal, India, where Mr Mallik plans to return to write his book.

Bhaskar Deb.description: Feluda's old classmate and a member of the Saturday Club, who provides information about Harinarayan.

Animesh Som.description: Feluda's old classmate and a member of the Bengal Club, who provides information about Devnarayan.

Harinarayan Acharya.description: Keertinarayan's second son and a chartered accountant with an interest in western classical music; his wife and daughter live in the Acharya household.

Statesman.description: A well-known English-language newspaper published in Kolkata.

daalmut.description: A crunchy Indian snack made from fried lentils and spices.

paddock.description: The area at a racecourse where horses are paraded before a race.

Haripada.description: Lalmohan Babu's driver, who assists in the surveillance operation.

Mozart.description: Famous Western composer referenced in the context of musical mysteries.

Salieri.description: Another composer, historically rumored to have poisoned Mozart.

Oriya.description: Refers to people or culture from Odisha, India; used here for the group's disguise.

paan.description: A betel leaf preparation chewed for its stimulant effects, common in India.

beedi.description: A thin, hand-rolled Indian cigarette made from tobacco wrapped in a tendu leaf.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment, a rectangular piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

shawl.description: A piece of fabric worn over the shoulders for warmth or as part of traditional attire.

twenty-nine.description: A popular card game played in India, especially in Bengal and Odisha.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in India, often paired with a dhoti or pyjama.

Turupo maruchi kain.description: An Oriya phrase used in the card game, meaning 'Are you playing a trump card?'

Tapesh.description: Feluda's cousin and assistant, who often narrates the stories and helps with the investigations.

Keertinarayan Acharya.description: Keertinarayan Acharya is the seventy-nine-year-old patriarch of the Acharya family and father of Indranarayan, Devnarayan, and Harinarayan, a retired barrister.

Mr Rebello.description: An antiques dealer who buys the Amati violin from Harinarayan Acharya.

Lowdon Street.description: A street name in the city, mentioned as a location Feluda visits.

Antonio Stradivari.description: A famous Italian violin maker from the seventeenth century.

Andrea Guarneri.description: Another renowned Italian violin maker from the seventeenth century.

Nicolo Amati.description: A celebrated Italian violin maker, the first to revolutionize violin making in Cremona.

Cremona.description: A city in Italy, famous for its tradition of violin making.

Happy Birthday.description: Another race horse's name, found on the same piece of paper.

Prakhar Rudra.description: A fictional hero created by Lalmohan Babu in his thriller novels.

The Three Musketeers.description: A reference to the famous novel by Alexandre Dumas, mentioned humorously by Lalmohan Babu.

pot-boilers.description: A term for works of literature or art produced quickly to make money rather than for artistic merit.
